steps: Choose the side being used as the base.
Find a segment from that base or its extension to the opposite vertex or side.
Check that the segment meets the base at $90^{\circ}$; this is the matching height.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Segment $h$ meets base $a$ at the marked right angle, so $h$ is its perpendicular height.
(b) Yes. Sides $a$ and $c$ are parallel, so $h$ is perpendicular to both. Side $s$ is slanted and does not meet either base at $90^{\circ}$.

The height runs from the opposite vertex $R$ to the line containing base $PQ$.
Extend $PQ$ to the marked right angle. Segment $t$ is the matching height, even though it is outside the triangle.

(a) Side $q$ meets base $p$ at $90^{\circ}$, so $q$ is the height.
(b) Side $p$ meets base $q$ at $90^{\circ}$, so $p$ is the height.
A side can be the height when it is perpendicular to the chosen base.

Segment $u$ meets the vertical base at the marked right angle and reaches the opposite side.
$u$ is the height. The height is horizontal because the chosen base is vertical.

workedExamples.question_text: A triangle and its chosen base-height pair are turned on the page without changing their size. Does the height change? Explain.
workedExamples.solution_text:
No. Turning the whole triangle preserves its lengths and angles.
The chosen base and its matching height turn together and still meet at $90^{\circ}$. Height does not mean vertical on the page.

Segment $k$ runs from the opposite vertex to base $b$ and meets it at the marked right angle.
$k$ is its perpendicular height. Side $s$ is not perpendicular to $b$.

foundation.solution_text: Segment $y$ meets the chosen base at the marked right angle and reaches the opposite side. The perpendicular height is $y$.

development.solution_text: Segment $d$ runs from the opposite vertex to base $a$ and meets it at the marked right angle. The perpendicular height is $d$.
Segment $q$ meets the top base at $90^{\circ}$ and reaches the extension of the opposite side. The perpendicular height is $q$.
Segment $t$ joins the opposite vertex to base $r$ at the marked right angle. The matching height is $t$.

mastery.solution_text:
Segment $e$ is perpendicular to the parallel sides $a$ and $c$.
Possible matching pairs are base $a$ with height $e$, or base $c$ with height $e$.

mastery.question_text:
An obtuse triangle has base $PQ$.
The perpendicular from $R$ misses segment $PQ$.
Explain how its height is still identified.
mastery.solution_text:
Extend the line containing base $PQ$.
Draw the segment from $R$ that meets this extended line at $90^{\circ}$.
That outside segment is the perpendicular height.
